# Constraint Contract

## Status and authority boundary

This is a constraint-source artifact only. It matures no plan by itself, grants no implementation authority, does not alter `CURRENT-AUTHORITY.json`, does not start Argo, and cannot support enrollment or a dogfood claim.

Binding inputs are:

- approved design `sha256:1a0d7b96fb4d4a35313355846a205bfd7c0f6c9fa093c957ba186f5b1bac0ba6`;
- Iliad pre-review `sha256:7b96f60ab9280c8c8173723f30892f4104583f5c9db17c44877bc724507ab634`;
- Daedalus methodology `sha256:9288e17e84b202e48c4dbfad13904abc9317bae22b82aeefa01ee6b837a0c406`;
- Daedalus comprehension result `sha256:d5e896f6be4cbcc92648f78a3e3adade9a70e52edd20f531c3be525b0ff693d3`;
- Eye file-ingress ruling `sha256:0c0e1e3c4930c768ac29af4006fb35af477dfa1892bc523f91b6865fc30f2ef4`;
- candidate plan `sha256:a84b65055b0dff79fa62f1e087d90faf5fc052f3439887881c96594b7c5e033f`.

The integrator must produce exactly one matrix row for every `PPC-W01` through `PPC-W29`. Each row must contain exactly `obligation_id`, `invariant`, `mechanism`, `task`, `negative_test`, and `exit_criterion`. Coverage is a strict bijection: no omission, invention, duplication, grouping, or aliasing.

A success string, object count, signature over a producer assertion, committed summary, stored-hash-to-stored-hash comparison, skipped matrix leg, or prose review is not proof.

## Smallest complete behavioral model

### Production lifecycle

The only states and forward transitions are:

```text
LEGACY_INACTIVE

ACTIVE_UNPREPARED --RECORD_INPUT--> INPUT_RECORDED
INPUT_RECORDED --COMPILE--> COMPILED
COMPILED --COMPLETE_WORKSHOP--> WORKSHOP_COMPLETE
WORKSHOP_COMPLETE --RECORD_PLAN--> PLANNED
PLANNED --PASS_GATE--> GATE_PASSED
GATE_PASSED --AUTHORIZE_BUILD--> AUTHORIZED_BUILD
AUTHORIZED_BUILD --SETTLE_ORDINARY--> ORDINARY_SETTLED
ORDINARY_SETTLED --PREPARE_EVIDENCE_FRONTIER--> EVIDENCE_FRONTIER_PREPARED
EVIDENCE_FRONTIER_PREPARED --SETTLE_VERIFICATION--> VERIFICATION_SETTLED
VERIFICATION_SETTLED --PASS_FINAL_PROFILE--> FINAL_PROFILE_PASSED
FINAL_PROFILE_PASSED --COMPLETE--> DONE
```

`LEGACY_INACTIVE` is selected only when every activation condition is false and has no transition into an active build. Skipped, repeated, reversed, unknown, or post-`DONE` transitions fail.

A blocker or cannot-run seals the invocation without advancing. Resume requires re-reading durable bytes and independently recomputing every state-specific reference. Any semantic profile, fact, source, obligation, policy, registry, executable, evidence, repository, or plan drift returns `new-revision-required`; a production `respec` likewise requires a new plan and fresh authorization.

The V2 authorization certificate is immutable pre-build evidence. Frontier and settlement records cannot edit or backdate it.

### Artifact replacement recovery

Before rename, any validation, serialization, write, fsync, containment, or capability failure preserves the old file byte-for-byte. After rename, parent-directory fsync failure is the sole `ATOMIC_REPLACEMENT_INDETERMINATE` internal detail under public `CANNOT_RUN`: only complete old or complete new canonical bytes may be visible. No lifecycle transition or second artifact may be written. A fresh invocation must re-derive old, new, and observed references: exact old retries; exact new succeeds only after a fresh parent fsync; missing, partial, unreadable, or third-party bytes remain cannot-run.

### Self-publication lifecycle

Each controller-derived contiguous `attempt-NNN` follows exactly:

```text
ABSENT -> PREPARED -> AUTHORIZED -> PUBLISHED
PREPARED|AUTHORIZED -> SUPERSEDED
```

`PUBLISHED` and `SUPERSEDED` are terminal. A signed append-only attempt-ledger event is the sole commit marker for its immutable directory. Pending or final directories without the matching marker are untrusted.

Unsafe recovery must durably install a signed exclusive `FORENSIC_HOLD`. While a valid hold exists, every mutating preparation, authorization, publication, recovery, or supersession mode blocks before key access. Only a separate Eye/TELOS change-protocol disposition may resolve it.

## Trust boundaries

| Boundary | Trusted input | Insufficient or hostile input | Required predicate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Authority | Exact matured-plan bytes, TELOS authorization, Eye implementation decision | Design approval, convergence, comprehension labels, filenames, consensus, self-host success | Hash-exact authorization and Argo entry before work |
| Controller to compiler | Closed dossier, signal resolutions, build mode, evidence bindings | Model prose, inferred defaults, waivers, `n/a`, unknown-accepted values | Closed validation before any model call |
| File ingress | Controller-declared `none` or admitted CSV/JSON/XLSX set; actual bytes | Filename, extension, MIME, archive label, model/classifier judgment | Bounded local byte validation before storage, model/tool use, or egress; inherited full data classification |
| Process to repository | Explicit physical root and safe relative paths | Ambient CWD, ignore files, absolute semantic paths, escaping links | Realpath containment, stable bounded reads, deterministic traversal |
| Artifact store | Canonical content-addressed bytes and signed ledger references | Mutable in-memory objects, current-view filenames, stored assertions | Re-read and re-hash at restart, proposal gate, execution, and settlement |
| Scanner to profile | Registered structured facts and current exact signal resolutions | Arbitrary text matches and unknown dependency semantics | Monotonic joins; unresolved signals block; partial scans discarded |
| Policy and registry | Validated local canonical policy and current closed source-bound registry | Remote packs, caller executables, host outcomes, stale implementations | Policy validation before scanning; current reference derivation |
| Workshop | Ordinary tasks within permitted writes | Production sources, reserved nodes, skips, policy choices, controller artifacts | Frozen summary, protected-write rejection, controller node minting |
| Runtime adapter | Literal loopback mappings and synthetic bindings | DNS, redirects, proxies, external URLs, adapter-owned outcomes | Policy-owned scenarios and registry-owned limits; candidate-handler trace |
| Structural evidence | Bounded JSON plus current source hashes | Prose, self-certified result, duplicate controls, YAML/HCL/Terraform | Exactly one control and registry-owned predicate |
| Process evidence | Public Ed25519 keyring and exact signed current record | Private key, unsigned declaration, stale/cross-plan record | Signature, source, check, plan, executing-build, freshness, and conflict verification |
| Ledger to process evidence | Recomputed plan, signed ordinary settlements, current disk trees | Plan intent or ledger-declared tree hash alone | Independently derive `executing_build_ref` |
| Authorization to execution | Certificate selected from recomputed plan | Caller-selected version or stale plan | V1/V2 plan-aware dispatch and repeated equality checks |
| Candidate to TELOS | Ordinary host lifecycle and separately approved dossier/plan | Repository-name branch, packet-only fixture, summary, direct ledger insertion | Same compiler, policy, registry, gate, scanner, checks, settlement, and `done()` |
| Public claims | Registered bounded predicate and exact evidence refs | Marketing prose, signature alone, promoted evidence tier | Closed claim vocabulary and mandatory non-claims |

The controller and build controller remain one trust principal in V1. Content addressing does not prove human authorship of dossier values.

## Closed normative contracts

All versioned objects have exact keys, exact value domains, `additionalProperties: false`, duplicate-key rejection, prototype-key rejection, fatal UTF-8 parsing, safe integers, valid Unicode, and no implicit defaults. Set arrays are duplicate-free and code-unit sorted. `none` is exclusive where permitted. Unknown fields, versions, operators, templates, kinds, claims, operations, and finding codes fail closed.

The Eye ruling adds `file_ingress_formats`, exactly `['none']` or a non-empty sorted subset of `['csv','json','xlsx']`. It adds exactly `FILE-INGRESS-001` in the existing data domain, using `production-loopback-http-v1`; therefore the frozen catalog contains 32 IDs, eleven domains, and eight check kinds.

The exact catalog is:

```text
AI-CLAIM-001 AI-DECISION-001 AI-EGRESS-001 AI-LINEAGE-001 AI-OPS-001
AI-OUTPUT-001 AI-PROVIDER-001 AI-RAG-001 AI-TENANT-001 AI-TOOL-001
AUTHN-001 AUTHN-002 AUTHZ-001 AUTHZ-002 DATA-001 DATA-002
DELIVERY-001 DELIVERY-002 FILE-INGRESS-001 OBS-001 OBS-002 PAY-001 PAY-002
PRIV-001 PRIV-002 PRIV-003 RECOVERY-001 RECOVERY-002 SCALE-001 SCALE-002
SUPPLY-001 SUPPLY-002
```

The exact registry is:

```text
production-loopback-http-v1 production-auth-boundary-v1
production-tenant-isolation-v1 production-rate-limit-v1 production-webhook-v1
production-ai-egress-v1 production-json-assertions-v1 production-record-v1
```

The runtime manifest operation set is exactly the design’s fourteen operations plus `file-admit`. It maps routes and bounded fixture bindings only; it cannot declare outcomes.

The public claim vocabulary is exactly:

```text
AI-CLAIM-AGENTIC-ACTIONS-001
AI-CLAIM-CONSEQUENTIAL-DECISIONING-001
AI-CLAIM-CUSTOMER-FACING-001
AI-CLAIM-INTERNAL-ASSISTANT-001
AI-CLAIM-RETRIEVAL-AUGMENTED-001
```

Compiler/lifecycle public findings are exactly the frozen 20-code `FINDING_CODES`. Publication recovery separately owns exactly:

```text
LEDGER_PREFIX_MISMATCH LOCK_STATE_UNSAFE MARKER_WITHOUT_DIRECTORY
PUBLICATION_BYTES_MISMATCH RECOVERY_STATE_UNSAFE
```

The vocabularies cannot be merged or substituted. Internal detail codes—including `ATOMIC_REPLACEMENT_INDETERMINATE` and missing-callback diagnostics—cannot occupy public finding fields.

Compiler exits are `0` success, `2` deterministic blocker, and `1` cannot-run, with cannot-run precedence. Check exits are `0` proved, `1` assertion failed, and `2` could not run safely. Every nonzero check blocks while preserving the distinction.

Every consumer recomputes content addresses from current canonical bytes. Required identities include production input, profile, semantic facts, policy and rules, parameter schema, implementation source closure, registry, runtime manifest, public process keyring, evidence configuration, sources, obligation set, V2 check contracts, production executables including `env_contract`, plan, executing build, frontier, settlement, process records, and publication artifacts. Stored-reference equality alone never suffices.

## Proof obligations

### PPC-W01 — Authority is external and hash-exact

No task, edit, callback, provider call, or slice event begins without authorization over the exact matured-plan bytes and successful Argo entry. This workshop changes no authority record.

Negative test: mutate one plan byte after producing an otherwise valid authorization. Verification must reject before any callback, edit marker, or slice event.

### PPC-W02 — Activation is exact and pre-model

Activation is true iff proposal lifecycle, market-bound, production profile presence, or production evidence presence triggers it. Activated builds require proposal lifecycle and a complete profile before convention detection or any model/workshop/council/team/decomposition call. All-false legacy behavior and bytes remain unchanged.

Negative test: exercise each trigger with an absent profile while counting every callback; the exact blocker must appear and all counts remain zero, while the all-false control follows the legacy path.

### PPC-W03 — Controller input and file-ingress declarations are closed

Only controller input sets facts, signal resolutions, evidence, and file-admission scope. All frozen cross-field, path, identifier, exclusivity, secret/personal-data, and `file_ingress_formats` rules apply. File-derived values inherit the complete top-level data-classification set; no classifier may lower it.

Negative test: add an unknown key, secret-shaped value, contradictory `none`, undeclared format, or lowered file-derived class. Validation must block without writing canonical input or calling a model.

### PPC-W04 — Canonicalization is deterministic and nonconstant

Equivalent semantics produce byte-identical artifacts and references on Node 18 and 20 independent of key/set/traversal order, line endings, locale, clock, root, or separator. A semantic mutation changes each identity containing it.

Negative test: compare permuted-equivalent fixtures across both Node versions, then flip one relevant scalar. Equivalents must match byte-for-byte; affected profile and global plan refs must differ after mutation.

### PPC-W05 — Artifact I/O is durable, contained, and reconstruction-only

Controller artifacts use bounded stable reads, physical containment, canonical bytes, content addresses, crash-durable atomic installation, and disk-only reconstruction. Controller artifacts and trust anchors are never model write targets.

Negative test: inject failures at temp fsync, rename, and parent fsync. Pre-rename failures preserve the sentinel; post-rename failure exposes only complete old/new bytes and enters the indeterminate state; restart old/new/neither cases respectively retry, fsync-then-succeed, and block.

### PPC-W06 — Scanning is bounded and all-or-nothing

The scanner is deterministic, read-only, network-free, policy-detector-bound, immune to host ignore suppression, and limited by registered paths and byte caps. Any unsafe path, alias, race, unreadable required file, malformed registered data, or limit failure discards all partial facts.

Negative test: emit one tentative fact, then encounter an escaping registered symlink. The result must be cannot-run with no accepted facts.

### PPC-W07 — Reconciliation is monotonic and signal-exact

Confirmed observations only union sets, raise ordered floors, or flip capabilities false-to-true. Text matches remain signals. Every resolution must name one exact current signal; missing, stale, fabricated, or duplicate resolutions and non-ordered contradictions block.

Negative test: combine an attempted lowering with a stale resolution. The higher controller declaration must remain effective, obligations remain present, and `STALE_SIGNAL_RESOLUTION` blocks.

### PPC-W08 — Policy and the 32-rule catalog are pinned and complete

The validated local policy is the only V1 policy and must load before scanning. It contains exactly the 32 IDs, eleven domains, frozen triggers, projections, tiers, check kinds, and required result `pass`. Each rule has non-trigger, one-fact trigger, pass, fail, and stale-identity fixtures.

Negative test: remove one rule and replace another operator with an unknown operator. Exact-set validation must fail, the scanner-read counter must remain zero for malformed policy, and neither a count nor false evaluation may pass.

### PPC-W09 — Evidence applicability and strength are exact

Every obligation has exactly one tier: runtime, structural, or process. Missing adapters, operations, artifacts, formats, or keyrings block without dropping the obligation. Reports cannot promote a weaker tier. Evidence configuration and trust-anchor bytes are authorization-bound.

Negative test: trigger runtime evidence with `runtime.kind: none` and provide structural JSON claiming success. The runtime obligation remains and compilation returns `EVIDENCE_ADAPTER_REQUIRED`.

### PPC-W10 — Registry execution is closed and implementation-bound

The registry has exactly eight kinds. Schemas, guards, limits, result semantics, environment contract, dispatcher, runner, redactor, entries, and transitive helpers determine implementation and registry refs. Callers cannot inject commands, outcomes, paths, environments, or implementation refs. Production execution uses exact bare `node`, `telos-scrubbed-v1`, and spawn-only `process.execPath` resolution.

Negative test: replace a check or status mapper with a passing no-op while retaining the stored contract. Current re-resolution must report stale contract/executable identity and refuse discharge.

### PPC-W11 — Runtime and file-admission evidence exercise bounded real behavior

Runtime checks use literal loopback HTTP, explicit ports, synthetic fixtures, fixed caps, no redirects/DNS/proxies/external sockets, policy-owned outcomes, and a trace proving the candidate handler ran. `file-admit` validates actual bytes before storage, model/tool use, or egress. JSON and CSV are bounded locally; XLSX is bounded OOXML and whole-workbook rejects images/media, macros, OLE/embeddings, external relationships, encryption, duplicate/traversing entries, malformed ZIP/XML, and unsupported relationships.

Negative test: return expected statuses without invoking the handler and admit PNG bytes renamed/MIME-labeled as JSON or embedded in XLSX. Trace binding and byte validation must fail; rejected inputs create zero durable-storage and egress events.

### PPC-W12 — Structural evidence proves only exact JSON artifacts

Structural checks require bounded canonical JSON, exactly one matching control across configured artifacts, current source path/hash equality, registry-owned predicates, and no self-citation. Unsupported formats block.

Negative test: duplicate a favorable control and mutate one referenced source byte. The check must fail/cannot-run rather than select the favorable record or trust its stored hash.

### PPC-W13 — Process evidence is externally signed and execution-bound

Process records require the closed schema, canonical signature preimage, authorized public Ed25519 key, exact obligation/source/check/plan/executing-build identities, current source hashes, result predicate, and freshness. Private keys never enter repository artifacts. Conflicting current records fail closed.

Negative test: replay a signed pass against another plan or mutate an ordinary artifact after settlement. Recomputed executing-build identity must differ and the record cannot discharge; a conflicting fail record cannot be ignored.

### PPC-W14 — Production obligations are typed V2 without legacy drift

Production sources use explicit obligation version 2 and `source_kind: production-policy`; they are not concerns. Unknown versions and source kinds fail. Legacy obligations omit the version and preserve exact historical obligation, check, executable, and obligation-free plan preimages.

Negative test: encode a production source as a concern and a legacy obligation with explicit version 1. Both fail while every pinned legacy golden remains byte-identical.

### PPC-W15 — Sources and obligations reconcile bijectively

Each production obligation maps to exactly one current compiler source and each legacy obligation to exactly one reconstructed concern. Class, ID, source ref, result, contract, discharge node, test, executable, and `verifies` registration must agree. Missing, extra, duplicate, orphan, and cross-bound entries block.

Negative test: duplicate one production source while deleting another so counts remain equal. Exact-set reconciliation must fail; map overwrite or count equality cannot pass.

### PPC-W16 — Production nodes are controller-owned

Models receive a frozen summary only. The controller alone mints reserved node IDs, empty writes, policy-derived reads, exact requirements, current registry tests, and dependencies on every captured ordinary task plus evidence producers. Review obligations may add but cannot replace production obligations.

Negative test: return workshop output containing a reserved `verify-production-*` node or a write to a controller keyring/artifact. Reject before graph compilation.

### PPC-W17 — Plan and certificate bind complete production state

Production lifecycle metadata is all-or-nothing and binds input, profile, facts, policy, registry, evidence, source set, compiled artifact, obligations, tests, and metadata into `plan_hash`. Production plans require policy certificate V2 with `production_profile: pass`; V1 and `n/a` are invalid.

Negative test: change only evidence configuration while replaying the old plan hash and certificate. Recomputed plan/certificate verification must fail; V1 downgrade and V2 `n/a` must also fail.

### PPC-W18 — Proposal verification is disk-only and current

After restart, the gate reconstructs the signed root, build intent, production input, evidence sidecar, compiled artifact, manifest, and keyring; it rescans and re-resolves current policy, registry, sources, checks, and executables. In-memory state, current-view files, and summaries cannot substitute.

Negative test: retain a valid in-memory compilation while replacing a disk input artifact or registry helper byte. Verification must emit the typed mismatch and issue no certificate.

### PPC-W19 — Failures and public vocabularies are closed

Reports use only their owning closed finding vocabulary, legal severity/status combinations, bounded redacted detail, and exact exit precedence. Cannot-run dominates blockers; advisory escalation never enters certificate findings. Nonzero paths do not replace successful artifacts or route to authorization. Internal diagnostics cannot escape as public codes.

Negative test: combine a profile blocker, scanner I/O failure, unknown public code, and sentinel output. Exit must be `1`, public code must remain `CANNOT_RUN`, internal detail stays internal/redacted, sentinel is unchanged, and routing cannot yield revise/authorized.

### PPC-W20 — Settlement requires current execution and complete discharge

The executing build derives from the recomputed plan, authorized signed ordinary settlements, and independently re-hashed current artifacts. Every exact discharge node must run its current registered test and exit zero. Generic verification and `done()` reject every undischarged obligation; exits 1 and 2 remain distinct but both block.

Negative test: mutate an ordinary artifact after settlement and make discharge checks exit 1 and 2. Executing-build derivation and `done()` must block while structured results preserve both statuses.

### PPC-W21 — Final facts and production respec invalidate stale authority

Immediately before final success, the controller recompiles from final disk state including declared untracked outputs. Any profile, fact, source, obligation, check, executable, evidence, lifecycle, or plan difference returns `BLOCKED_PROFILE_DRIFT`. Production `respec` cannot mutate and continue under the old certificate.

Negative test: add a confirmed provider dependency during the build. Final verification must block, preserve the old certificate, dispatch no green completion, and require a fresh plan and authorization.

### PPC-W22 — The process frontier is durable and non-certifying

After ordinary settlement and before discharge, the controller verifies an exact existing frontier or invokes the external frontier once. The frontier binds plan, executing build, configured record paths, and exact raw bytes but does not certify record semantics. Missing/throwing callbacks, partial evidence, stale artifacts, unauthorized writes, and invalid shapes block before discharge.

Negative test: restart with a current-plan frontier whose evidence file changed by one byte. It must not be reused, overwritten, or silently repaired, and no discharge node may run.

### PPC-W23 — All activated consumers and fresh hosts use one lifecycle

Every genuine proposal-lifecycle or market-bound consumer, including both forges, enters production preparation and V2 authorization. Readiness helpers are non-authorizing. A neutral host needs no TELOS authority or institutional-memory files; missing triggered evidence yields typed blockers.

Negative test: supply green readiness packets to a market-bound forge without a profile and count legacy/model calls; it must block before them. A neutral fresh-host fixture must compile, then return the exact blocker when its required adapter is removed.

### PPC-W24 — The synthetic demonstration proves bounded file and egress controls

The committed demonstration traverses the real compiler, planner, gate, checks, settlement, and `done()` path. It uses only synthetic fixtures, literal loopback, and invalid marker `000-00-0000`. It proves declared benign JSON/CSV/XLSX admission, rejection of disguised/image-bearing/unsafe workbooks before storage or egress, unsafe AI egress failure with one redacted loopback attempt, corrected blocking before transport, redacted audit output, and profile escalation invalidating authorization.

Negative test: re-derive from source artifacts after mutating byte inspection to extension-only acceptance, corrected egress to one transport attempt, or before/after plan hashes to equality. Verification must fail without trusting the summary.

### PPC-W25 — TELOS self-hosting has no privileged path

TELOS uses an Eye-approved tracked dossier and separately authorized self-host plan through the ordinary compiler, policy, registry, proposal reconstruction, V2 certificate, checks, final scan, discharge, and `done()` path. It restarts from disk, uses no live provider or real personal data, and leaves the checkout clean. Repository identity and the packet-only fixture are insufficient.

Negative test: independently remove an obligation, substitute a no-op, lower confirmed egress/write/execute, and add a confirmed provider fact. Each must block; renaming the repository must not change the result.

### PPC-W26 — Self-publication is immutable, signed, and fail-closed in recovery

Controller, process, and attempt-governance keys are distinct external Ed25519 keys. Attempts and artifacts are write-once; the signed append-only attempt ledger is the commit marker. Prefixes, transitions, IDs, keyrings, and manifests are independently verified. Unsafe recovery durably creates a forensic hold and cannot become supersession or success.

Negative test: inject crashes at every directory/ledger fsync and rename boundary, then create a marker/bytes mismatch. Recovery must install and verify the hold before exit 1; every later mutating mode blocks before key access, and deleting/forging the hold cannot restore operation.

### PPC-W27 — Runtime and host portability are fail-closed

New runtime code is Node 18/20 ESM with only `node:` and repository-relative imports and zero dependencies. It uses no shell assembly, ambient credentials, live provider calls, or real personal data. Paths are portable and physically contained. Production children receive only the ten-key scrubbed environment intersection and controller runtime executable.

Negative test: place fake `node` first in `PATH`, add credential/proxy/canary variables, and inject an external package import. Production execution must use the controller runtime, expose no canary, contact no external service, and fail the complete plan-derived transitive import audit.

### PPC-W28 — Lifecycle evidence and enrollment order are executable

Commit-anchored evidence must cover pre-review; exact two-parent parallel Daedalus authorship; the exact 29-row matrix; authorization of the matured hash; Argo entry and append-only slices; reference documentation; committed self-hosting; Clotho weave; post-review; retrospective; independent lifecycle verification; and only then enrollment. Superseded evidence remains. Dogfood and enrollment require the prior green self-run.

Negative test: remove/stale-bind one Daedalus parent, one matrix row, a slice event, self publication, retrospective, or lifecycle-verification ancestor while leaving enrollment prose present. The institutional oracle must fail.

### PPC-W29 — Claims cannot exceed independently executed predicates

Machine summaries, documentation, institutional records, and acceptance artifacts claim only registered bounded predicates independently re-derived from exact bytes. Runtime, structural, and process tiers remain distinct. All explicit non-claims remain mandatory. Producer statuses, signatures, CI conclusions, and summaries are assertions rather than pass inputs.

Negative test: add an unknown claim ID, promote a structural result to runtime proof, broaden a statement to secure/compliant/certified, or flip all producer statuses to pass while retaining stale evidence. Publication, institutional, and acceptance verification must still fail.

## Preservation verdict rule

The constraints verifier may return literal `preserved` only when all 29 rows form the exact bijection, every controller-jurisdiction mechanism remains controller-owned, every negative test is executable and produces its specified failure, all schemas and vocabularies remain closed, hashes are re-derived from bytes, and no evidence or claim exceeds its executable predicate. Any hidden skip, stale-hash acceptance, self-certified evidence, open schema, missing negative control, broadened claim, or weakened Eye ruling is `violated` and routes to The Eye.
